name: Nasher Sculpture Center
funding: No donor list is published. Its credit line names only TACA, the Texas Commission on the Arts, and unnamed members and donors. FY2025 revenue was $14.0M, nearly all contributions.
watch: Private collection gifted to the public in Dallas's arts district.
records_note: Seven trustees are named on its site and Form 990s from 2003 to 2025 are on ProPublica; no annual report or donor list was found.

name: Des Moines Art Center
funding: It paid artist Mary Miss $900,000 to settle her 2024 lawsuit.
watch: Miss sued in April 2024 to stop removal of Greenwood Pond: Double Site; removal began in February 2025. An artist-rights dispute, not about funders.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2009 to 2025, Form 990s for 2013 to 2024, a 2025 donor list by gift level and 22 trustees.

name: Le Consortium
funding: Ministry of Culture and DRAC, City of Dijon, Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, Côte-d'Or council. Private partners: DVF, Groupe Roger Martin, art foundations, Friends of Le Consortium.
watch: Artist-led contemporary art center (Centre d'art contemporain d'intérêt national).
records_note: Names its public funders, Friends and main private supporters, and lists the association's three-person executive board; no annual reports or accounts are posted.

name: Jameel Arts Centre
funding: Privately funded by Art Jameel, the cultural arm of the Saudi group Abdul Latif Jameel. Not financed or run by the UAE state.
watch: Independent contemporary arts institution on Dubai Creek. Funded through the Jameel family philanthropic foundation; free public admission with emphasis on community learning and environmental research.
records_note: Neither the centre's site nor parent Art Jameel's site publishes annual reports, accounts, a funder list or a board.

name: Temple Bar Gallery + Studios
funding: Arts Council is principal funder. Grants from Dublin City Council, Culture Ireland and others; corporate partners Henry J Lyons, Arthur Cox and Dublin Port; RTÉ Supporting the Arts.
watch: Artist-founded and artist-led non-profit trust in central Dublin.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2025 audited accounts and a 13-member board, and names its Arts Council principal funder, grant funders and three corporate partners, undated.

name: Dundee Contemporary Arts
funding: £2.8M income (FY2025). Creative Scotland and Dundee; University of Dundee partner; supporters include Paul Hamlyn, Art Fund, Garfield Weston, Henry Moore Foundation, Screen Scotland, Whyte & Mackay.
watch: Baillie Gifford is not among its supporters. No protest, boycott or flagged funder found.
records_note: Annual report and accounts for 2024-25 are on its site and OSCR; funders appear as footer logos only; trustees are listed.

name: Towner Eastbourne
funding: £3.6M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £538k, Eastbourne Borough Council £414k (2024), Newhaven Enterprise Zone, Rick Mather David Sieff Foundation, Fidelity Foundation, Art Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund.
records_note: Annual reviews 2020-21 to 2024-25 are on its blog; accounts are on the Charity Commission register; funders show as logos; the board is listed.

name: Fruitmarket Gallery
funding: £1.6M. Creative Scotland Regular Funding, City of Edinburgh Council, trusts and patrons.
watch: Dropped Baillie Gifford in 2024 under pressure.
why_flagged: Dropped Baillie Gifford in 2024 under pressure.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, files returns with the Scottish charity regulator, names current supporters without a date, and lists its board.

name: Inverleith House (Royal Botanic Garden)
funding: £0.8M art program. Scottish Government environment directorate, Outset, Paul Mellon Centre.
watch: Ecological research institution; fully zero-carbon public governance.

name: National Galleries of Scotland
funding: £24M. Scottish Government grant-in-aid, Baillie Gifford, trusts and individual patrons.
watch: Kept Baillie Gifford under protest; dropped BP 2019.
why_flagged: Kept Baillie Gifford under protest; dropped BP 2019.
records_note: It posts audited accounts for 2023-24, names corporate supporters and donors on site pages, and OSCR lists its 12 trustees.

name: Art Gallery of Alberta
funding: Revenue C$6.3M in 2023, 46% government. Capital Power has been lead sponsor since 2010 and renewed in January 2023 with the Capital Power Indigenous Art Fund.
watch: Civic art museum in Edmonton. Tri-level public funding provides core stability; corporate partners (such as regional credit unions) are subject to public municipal gift guidelines.
why_flagged: Revenue C$6.3M in 2023, 46% government. Capital Power has been lead sponsor since 2010 and renewed in January 2023 with the Capital Power Indigenous Art Fund.
records_note: It posts yearly reports for 2020 to 2025 that name 2025 donors, lists its board, and files with Canada's charity regulator.

name: Van Abbemuseum
funding: Eindhoven municipality, Mondriaan Fund, Ammodo, Creative Europe and the Promotors foundation; VriendenLoterij, a public charity lottery, is also listed as a supporter.
watch: Operates the 'Deviant Practice' research programme, interrogating collection archives through decolonial, queer, and disability-inclusive perspectives. In 2021, Van Abbemuseum formally ratified a climate and ethical governance manifesto prohibiting corporate sponsorships from carbon-intensive, arms-manufacturing, or human-rights-flagged entities.
records_note: It names funds and donors on undated pages, but posts only 2012 and 2013 annual reports, no accounts and no board.
